07.08.2023

The present writ petition has been filed for issuance of direction upon the concerned respondents to recover the compensation amount illegally paid to the respondent no. 4 with regard to acquisition of land appertaining to plot nos. 100/1, 102, 105, 127/2, 171/2, Khata No. 08, Mouza- Patharia, P.S.No. 230, Circle- Madhupur, District- Deoghar measuring total area of 1.789 acres, vide Award No. 04 in connection with Land Acquisition Case No. 34 of 2019-20 for construction of overbridge on National Highway 114-A.

Further prayer has been made for issuance of direction upon the respondent authorities to refer the dispute before the competent authority under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (in short, "the Act, 2013") for adjudication.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. A counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of the respondent nos. 2 and 3 stating that the petitioner's objection against the aforesaid award was considered and disposed of on 06.09.2021 by the District Land Acquisition Officer, Deoghar-cum-Collector under the Act, 2013 (the respondent no. 3) after providing ample opportunity of hearing to the parties observing that according to Santhal Tribal Law, only male members can inherit the land being successors of their father.
If the brothers are co-sharers in a holding and one brother dies without issue, surviving brothers and the sons of pre-deceased brother inherit his share.

Accordingly, the petitioner being female member of Rupani Devi vs The State Of Jharkhand Through The ... on 7 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60907348/
1 the family has not been found entitled to receive share in compensation.

sentences.text: 3. However, a copy of order dated 06.09.2021 passed by the respondent no. 3 has not been annexed with the counter affidavit.
4. Be that as it may.

This Court is of the view that pursuant to objection filed by the petitioner before the respondent no. 3, he was not supposed to adjudicate the petitioner's claim on merit, rather he should have taken recourse of Section 64 of the Act, 2013 by referring the matter to the Authority constituted under Section 51 of the said Act for adjudication of the claim.

5. Under the aforesaid facts and circumstance, the respondent no. 3 is directed to refer the matter under Section 64 of the Act, 2013 to the Authority constituted under Section 51 of the said Act within one month from the date of receipt/production of a copy of this order.
6. The writ petition is accordingly disposed of with aforesaid direction.

(Rajesh Shankar, J.) Ritesh/
